why: Audit F-39, built as MI-231 under WO-20260909-DECISION-PACKAGES-CLOSED-WHILE-HOLDING-OPEN-LEGS (operator answered 2026-09-09, chosen: detector_and_reattach, Tier-2). TWO DELIVERABLES, and they are different facts. (a) DETECTOR: INV-PACKAGE-LEG-REACHABLE promotes package_leg_coverage.verdict in {stranded, divergent} into system_invariants.py so it lands in the suite's EXIT CODE rather than only in a latch file. It does NOT re-derive the verdict -- it imports package_leg_coverage.assess, the module's declared single owner ('one assessor, two consumers'), and reports not_measured rather than falling back to an inline copy. OBSERVED FAILING, not asserted: against the live payloads it exits 1 and names all four legs including real-money bybit_2 trade 5474; on a planted stranded leg it exits 1 and exits 0 once the package status is flipped back, one field apart. ⚠️ THE LOAD-BEARING DESIGN POINT, MEASURED HERE RATHER THAN INHERITED: /api/diag/journal is hard-clamped to _MAX_LIMIT=1000 rows ordered id DESC, so the live window ran 4618..5617 while stranded leg 4347 (alpaca_paper/SPY, open since 2026-08-03) sat BELOW it -- one of the four legs F-39 names, absent from the very payload the suite's docstring lists. A journal-only reading would have graded it CLEAN, reproducing F-37's class inside the fix for F-39. The invariant therefore also reads /api/bot/positions as the authoritative open book and recovers the package from order_packages.linked_trade_id; self-test case (f4) asserts the journal-only view reports it clean, so if the open-book cross-check ever stops being load-bearing the suite says so instead of going quietly green. 'Restricted to LIVE legs' is honoured by RECOMPUTING over the current open book and never reading the latch, whose clear path is unreachable once a package's last leg closes (F-38: 17 of 20 entries were ghosts, oldest 22 days); case (f7) pins that a fully-closed package does not fail the suite. linked_unresolvable is counted and named but is NOT a FAIL -- 'we could not look' must no more read as a violation than as a pass -- and it independently reproduced the audit's own excluded row, trade 4195/IEF. (b) RE-ATTACH: NOT APPLIED. All four legs re-read live and all four are still open AND backed by a real venue position (bybit_2 XRPUSDT 58.5, bybit_portfolio 11903.8, alpaca_paper SPY 11.0 and TLT 707.0), each matching its journal row exactly -- so none is a reconcile-as-closed case, and note two packages closed with exchange_flat_reconciled while the exchange holds precisely that position. The script requires a captured exchange_positions payload and REFUSES without it; an unreadable account is a refusal, never a flat; every target carries its expected current signature so it is safe to re-run and safe against a moved DB. 7 planted controls, six of them refusals, on the REAL schema built via Database() -- the first cut used a hand-rolled schema, passed the dry-run tests and failed under --apply with 'no such column: created_at', i.e. green while proving nothing about the write path. NO ORDER PLACED, MODIFIED OR CANCELLED on any account; no resting leg cancelled (BL-20260820); no env var changed; no venue touched. Deliberately NOT fixed: the sibling-leg gap (BL-20260818-MONITOR-MANAGES-ONLY-THE-LINKED-LEG, Tier-3 order path) -- re-attaching restores the package, not sibling management. ⚠️ REPORTED, NOT FIXED: system_invariants.py has NO scheduled caller and its self-test runs in no workflow (measured with a positive control: check_collapsed_states resolves to six CI files, system_invariants to none), which the 2026-09-09 audit already names as its highest-leverage change -- so this PR also adds tests/test_system_invariants_selftest.py, asserting the self-test's RETURN CODE from pytest-run, a REQUIRED branch-protection context, plus a negative control requiring the suite to exit 1 on a planted violation. That arms the planted controls; it does NOT schedule the suite against the fleet, and nothing here should be read as claiming it does.
